horizon_error.assumption: The whole horizon profile is shifted up or down by the stated angle, the same at every azimuth and for every observer height. 'Certain' holds even with the horizon that much higher than computed; 'possible' needs it that much lower. Other error sources (ephemeris, landing position, observer height) are not in this band.

landing_ellipse.assumption: The landing point may be anywhere inside the stated ellipse on the reference sphere. The sample points fill the ellipse evenly in area (sunflower pattern, the centre first). Every point has its own terrain horizon and its own local vertical. The share of points is a survey of the ellipse, not a probability, and it is not combined with the horizon error.

calendar.definition: A lunar day begins when the Sun crosses the 180 degree meridian of the body-fixed frame (the middle of the far side, close to new Moon). The periods do not depend on the site. The first and the last period are cut by the ends of the computed range.
